ga_lost_wall_north.blurb: Lost Wall North is a sandstone cliff on Pigeon Mountain in the northwest corner of the state, set among the hardwoods above the valley and tall enough for real multi-move leads. The climbing is mostly trad, with fist cracks, roofs and vertical faces, plus a handful of bolted lines. Grades run from easy 5.6 up to 5.12, but the weight sits in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, so it suits climbers stepping into leading as well as those with a full rack and some patience. Guzzler and Black Pig, both 5.8, are the ones people tend to seek out. Expect a forested, quiet setting with no services nearby.

ga_cherokee_bluffs.blurb: Cherokee Bluffs is a small bouldering area in a county park near Flowery Branch, northeast of Atlanta. The boulders and overhanging walls sit in the woods along a ridge, away from the main park buildings. Most problems are easy to moderate, with a smaller group of V4 to V7 lines and a few harder ones around the main roof. Dunk it, Slip n slide, Slip and Slide Low, Splash and The Nets are the better-known lines. Quality is mixed: low on the wall there are hollow, crumbly flakes that keep breaking, so test holds before trusting them, while the top-outs are solid. Walkers use the same trails, so it can feel busy.
ga_cherokee_bluffs.parking_note: Use the park's main lot. The boulders are in the woods behind the hiking trail, down and to the left once you pass the parked cars.

id_main_wall_3.blurb: The Main Wall is the biggest section of the Sunny Side cliffs at Ross Park in Pocatello, a short band of basalt right beside the road. Routes are numbered along the base and mostly short, with plenty of bolted leads and a good number of top-rope lines that have fixed anchors at the top. Grades start around 5.7 and run up to 5.12, with the greatest concentration between 5.9 and 5.11, so there is something for most levels. The wall takes strong sun and gets hot in summer afternoons, which is when climbers move over to the shadier cliffs nearby; mornings and cooler seasons are more comfortable.

id_black_slabbath_area.blurb: A cluster of basalt boulders toward the far end of the Swan Falls bouldering area, in the Snake River canyon south of Kuna. Most of the problems are easy to moderate, with a steady supply from VB to V4, but the area also holds a strong group of harder lines in the V6 to V8 range and a couple of real testpieces beyond that. Black Slabbath and Flaky Sidepulls are the friendlier problems; Surgery, Power Man, The Austrian and California love are the harder ones. The area is open desert with little shade, so spring, fall and winter days are best, and midsummer is too hot.
id_black_slabbath_area.approach: From the pullout, follow a faint trail up and to the left toward the large blocky boulder or the egg-shaped slab.

id_east_car_body_canyon.blurb: East Car Body Canyon is a basalt alcove above the Boise River on the Black Cliffs, a short drive east of town on Highway 21. The columnar rock offers natural cracks and a mix of trad, sport and a few top-rope lines, with grades from 5.6 into the 5.11s and the greatest number at 5.9 and 5.10. Macabre Roof, The Scream and Holiday in Cambodia are among the sought-after lines, alongside Curt's Boot at 5.7 and Neon Leprechaun at 5.10a. The wall faces west, so it is pleasantly shaded in the morning and a good choice in hot weather, with river views from the base.
id_east_car_body_canyon.approach: A short path leads to either side of the alcove.

id_red_light_district.blurb: Red Light District is a busy sport crag at Massacre Rocks, on basalt walls above the Snake River plain. It has three closely spaced sections: a tall left wall, a middle wall of 60 to 70 feet where many of the best lines sit, and a shorter right side. The climbing is steep and sustained with edges and pockets, and the grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, mostly between 5.10 and 5.12. Scared Stiff and Immaculate Deception are two of the standouts. It has one of the shortest walks in the area. Late fall and early spring are best; summer is hot and calls for early morning or evening starts.
id_red_light_district.parking_note: Two parking spots on the west rim of the canyon serve the crag, one for each end of the wall.
id_red_light_district.approach: The right-hand side is a short hike from the rim lot, and the left-hand side takes a little longer.

id_eagle_wall_left_center.blurb: The left and center portions of Eagle Wall, one of the larger sport crags at Massacre Rocks. The basalt is steep and featured with edges, pockets and slopers, and every route is bolted. The grades are concentrated in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with only a few easier lines like Flies On A Hotdog and Rap-Tour at 5.10a. Wildfire, Fire Away and Tour de Pump are among the better-known lines. Some descents need two ropes, so bring a long enough rope. The wall faces west, and summer is very hot, so cooler months or evenings are far better.
